column1: Valid Palindrome — given a string `s`, return True if it is a palindrome after lowercasing and removing all non-alphanumeric characters. Example: s='A man, a plan, a canal: Panama' → True; s='race a car' → False.
column2: PATTERN: Two pointers from both ends. | INSIGHT: Skip invalid chars on both sides, compare lowercased. | STEPS: 1) l=0, r=len(s)-1. 2) While l<r: while l<r and not s[l].isalnum(): l+=1; same for r; if s[l].lower()!=s[r].lower() → False; l+=1, r-=1. 3) Return True. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Re-check l<r inside the inner skip loops to avoid crossing.

column1: Is Subsequence — given strings `s` and `t`, return True if s is a subsequence of t (i.e., s can be obtained by deleting some characters of t without reordering). Example: s='abc', t='ahbgdc' → True; s='axc', t='ahbgdc' → False.
column2: PATTERN: Two pointers, advance both. | INSIGHT: Walk t; advance s only on a match. Done when s is exhausted. | STEPS: 1) i=j=0. 2) While i<len(s) and j<len(t): if s[i]==t[j]: i+=1; j+=1. 3) Return i==len(s). | TIME/SPACE: O(len(t)) / O(1). | PITFALL: Follow-up "many s queries" → preprocess t into dict[char]→sorted index list, then binary search.

column1: Two Sum II Input Array Is Sorted — given a 1-indexed sorted array `numbers` and integer `target`, return the 1-based pair [i,j] (i<j) of numbers summing to target. Exactly one solution; constant extra space. Example: numbers=[2,7,11,15], target=9 → [1,2].
column2: PATTERN: Two pointers from ends on a sorted array. | INSIGHT: If sum too small, only moving left pointer right can grow it; mirror for too big. | STEPS: 1) l=0, r=n-1. 2) Loop: s = nums[l]+nums[r]; if s==target → [l+1,r+1]; if s<target l+=1 else r-=1. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Return is 1-indexed.

column1: Container With Most Water — given an integer array `height` where height[i] is a vertical line at x=i, find two lines that with the x-axis form a container holding the most water. Return the max area. Example: height=[1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7] → 49 (lines at index 1 and 8).
column2: PATTERN: Two pointers shrinking. | INSIGHT: Width always shrinks, so the only chance to gain area is taller height — always move the SHORTER side inward. | STEPS: 1) l=0, r=n-1, best=0. 2) Loop: best=max(best, (r-l)*min(h[l],h[r])); if h[l]<h[r]: l+=1 else r-=1. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Moving the taller side can never improve the answer — proof by contradiction is the standard interview ask.

column1: 3Sum — given an integer array `nums`, return ALL unique triplets [a,b,c] with a+b+c=0. The result must not contain duplicate triplets. Example: nums=[-1,0,1,2,-1,-4] → [[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]].
column2: PATTERN: Sort + fix one + two pointers + dedup. | INSIGHT: After sorting, fix nums[i]; reduce to Two Sum II on the suffix. Skip duplicates at THREE places. | STEPS: 1) Sort. 2) For i in range(n-2): if i>0 and nums[i]==nums[i-1] continue; if nums[i]>0 break; l=i+1, r=n-1; two-pointer on target=-nums[i]; on hit, append and skip dup l/r. | TIME/SPACE: O(n²) / O(1) extra. | PITFALL: Forgetting any of the 3 dedup skips → duplicate triplets.
